content.text: Four EQE points place the peak between Sb 0.26 and 0.50, and XRD shows samples 3 and 5 have the same pyrochlore-like phase. I'm using my last EQE measurement on index 4 (Sb 0.362).

input.rationale: Highest measured EQE was 0.0178% at Sb 0.33, on the Pb-rich side of the Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore-like phase. EQE falls off sharply on both sides: 0.0106% at 0.362, 0.0018% at 0.264 and 0.0012% at 0.50. It is almost zero at 0.68 (Sb-rich, PbSb2O6 region). XRD shows the same pyrochlore-like pattern at 0.33 and 0.397, so the change in EQE is not caused by a change of phase.

content.text:
I submitted **index 3 (Sb fraction 0.33)** as the best composition. At 0.0178% it had the highest EQE of the five compositions I measured. I used all 5 EQE measurements and 2 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.264 | 0.0018 |
| **3** | **0.330** | **0.0178** |
| 4 | 0.362 | 0.0106 |
| 8 | 0.502 | 0.0012 |
| 14 | 0.684 | ~0 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE drops sharply on both sides of 0.33. I didn't measure index 1 (0.285) or index 2 (0.305), so the true peak could be slightly lower in Sb than 0.33 and a bit higher than what I found. The gap between 0.33 and 0.36 is ruled out, because index 4 came in lower.
- **Crystal structure:** XRD at 0.33 and 0.397 gave nearly the same pattern, which looks like the Pb₂Sb₂O₇ pyrochlore-type phase. So the change in EQE across that range doesn't come from a change of phase. I identified the phase from the peak positions only; I didn't run the pattern-matching tool to confirm it.
- **Sb-rich side:** EQE is essentially zero at 0.68 (the PbSb₂O₆ region), so compositions from there up to 0.92 are very unlikely to compete.

All EQE values are low, well under 0.1%, so this system is a weak photoanode at 2.1 eV illumination.
